questions.question: A class-aware NMS pass has already kept a person box with score 0.92. A second person box has score 0.78 and IoU 0.738 with it. What happens when the NMS IoU threshold is 0.50?
options: The 0.78 box is suppressed because 0.738 is greater than 0.50
Both boxes are kept because both scores exceed 0.50
The 0.92 box is suppressed because it overlaps the later box
Both boxes are removed because their IoU is non-zero
questions.explanation: Traditional NMS processes higher scores first and removes a lower-scoring same-class box when its IoU with a kept box is greater than the configured threshold.

questions.question: What is the usual effect of lowering a traditional NMS IoU threshold while holding candidate boxes and scores fixed?
options: More overlapping lower-score boxes are suppressed
More low-confidence candidates pass the confidence filter
The model evaluates more input pixels
Different classes are merged into one class
questions.explanation: A lower IoU threshold makes the overlap test stricter, so a smaller overlap is enough to suppress a lower-score box. It does not change the model forward pass or confidence filter.

questions.question: Why can an overlapping pallet box and forklift box both survive class-aware NMS?
options: Class-aware NMS compares boxes within the same class rather than suppressing across classes
IoU is defined only for boxes with identical coordinates
Confidence scores cannot be compared across images
NMS always keeps exactly one box per image
questions.explanation: Class-aware NMS runs suppression separately per class. A class-agnostic pipeline is a different policy and can remove overlaps across labels.

questions.question: A batch contains four 640 x 640 RGB FP16 input tensors, and the pipeline keeps two staging copies. How much raw input storage is accounted for?
options: 37.5 MiB
4.69 MiB
questions.explanation: The exact storage is 4 x 640 x 640 x 3 x 2 bytes x 2 copies / 1,048,576 = 18.75 MiB. Model weights, activations, runtime workspace, and allocator overhead are separate.

questions.question: After changing input resolution or batch size, why should an operator re-profile latency and non-input memory on the target runtime?
options: Those values depend on the exported graph, shapes, runtime, hardware, and workload rather than a universal YOLO multiplier
NMS changes the physical GPU memory capacity
The class labels become invalid at a new resolution
All YOLO variants have the same measured latency
questions.explanation: Shape and batch changes can alter kernels, activations, workspace, transfers, and queue behavior. Trust measurements from the actual export and deployment path, not generic family-level claims.

questions.question: Which statement correctly scopes the role of NMS in the YOLO family?
options: Many traditional YOLO pipelines use NMS, while some explicitly designed end-to-end variants are NMS-free
Every YOLO implementation is required to use the same class-aware NMS code
The original YOLO paper defined every modern framework's post-processing API
NMS is part of image resizing rather than detection post-processing
questions.explanation: NMS is common in traditional detector pipelines, but it is not a timeless invariant of every model carrying the YOLO name. Verify the chosen model and export contract.

questions.question: What is the strongest production release gate for confidence and IoU thresholds?
options: Evaluate end-to-end precision, recall, duplicate behavior, and latency on representative labeled slices
Keep the framework defaults for every domain
Choose the threshold that produces the fewest boxes on one image
Use the model's parameter count as a substitute for validation
questions.explanation: Thresholds encode product costs. They must be selected against representative labeled data, important slices, and the full preprocessing and post-processing path.
